title: Spurious zero-dispersion continua in full $(2,q)$-positivity: A linear hierarchy-depth lower bound from an exactly solvable counting operator
abstract: Variational two-particle reduced-density-matrix methods impose hierarchies of semidefinite constraints. We ask whether a fixed level of such a hierarchy can recover even an elementary many-fermion spectrum, using   the dispersion test, in which a value is accepted as an eigenvalue when the minimized dispersion vanishes. For an exactly solvable operator that counts fermions in one half of the spin orbitals, whose spectrum   consists of integers, we determine the complete set of accepted values at every level of the full hierarchy of particle-hole semidefinite constraints. Besides the integers, this set contains an entire interval of   noninteger values unless the hierarchy level grows linearly with the particle number, and we give the exact threshold. The proof constructs explicit pseudo reduced density matrices that are diagonal in the   occupation basis, obtained by continuing the occupation probabilities of a fixed-particle-number state to a noninteger particle number. Classical semidefinite constraints on occupation correlations, supplemented by   nonnegative occupation-pattern probabilities, suffice to establish fermionic positivity. For this counting model the two relaxations have the same dispersion zero set, not necessarily the same feasible states, and a   converse argument shows that no other false eigenvalues occur. The limitation is specific to the hierarchy: two-body inequalities that encode the integer spectrum would remove every false value but are not generated   at a fixed level. We also verify that the full semidefinite constraints and their complete projection onto two-particle reduced-density-matrix space are equivalent in finite dimensions, so that the result applies   equally to the polar formulation.
summary: This theoretical paper analyzes the mathematical constraints imposed on many-fermion systems when using approximate reduced density matrices. It shows that imposing positivity constraints up to a fixed level $q$ can incorrectly predict the existence of noninteger eigenvalues (spurious continua) for certain operators. The work provides an exact threshold for when these approximations fail, guiding the development of more robust theoretical methods for strongly correlated materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates the spurious zero-dispersion continua that can arise when approximating the spectrum of many-fermion systems using variational reduced density matrices (RDMs) subject to semidefinite constraints.
main_result: It determines the exact set of accepted eigenvalues for a solvable counting operator at every level of the full hierarchy of particle-hole constraints, showing that false noninteger eigenvalues appear unless the constraint level grows linearly with particle number.
method: The analysis employs the 'dispersion test' on an exactly solvable counting operator, constructing pseudo reduced density matrices by analytically continuing occupation probabilities to noninteger particle numbers.
model_or_system: The study concerns fermionic many-body systems, using the framework of reduced density matrices and imposing constraints derived from full $(2, q)$-positivity conditions.
key_observables: The set of accepted eigenvalues for the counting operator, the minimized dispersion, and the occupation-correlation matrices.
important_parameters: The hierarchy level $q$ (positivity order), the particle number $N$, and the orbital basis size $r$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the validity of the full hierarchy of semidefinite constraints and relies on constructing pseudo-reduced density matrices via signed interpolation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the constraints imposed by full $(2, q)$-positivity, establishing equivalences between polar and full formulations, and then applies this framework to a solvable counting model to pinpoint the exact spectrum and the conditions under which spurious eigenvalues appear.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of N-representability constraints and the identification of systematic failure modes (spurious continua) are crucial for developing reliable theoretical tools for strongly correlated electron systems.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Explicit false continua for full (2, 3)-, (2, 4)-, and (2, 5)-positivity. Open circles mark the exact integer spectrum; the thick segment is the relaxed zero interval; and the cross marks the half-integer midpoint, where the exact dispersion is 1/4 and the relaxed value is zero.

FIG. 2. Minimal full-three-positivity failure. The exact dis- persion energy is the squared distance to the integer spectrum. Full order-three positivity has zero energy at every point of [2, 3], including λ = 5/2, where the exact value is 1/4.

FIG. 3. Zero sets from Theorem 2 for N = 15. Increasing q recovers integer spectral points from the two edges, while a central false continuum remains until the linear threshold q = 9 of Eq. (44), where the zero set equals the spectrum.
